category_title: Struggling readers who use collaborative talk to clarify text confusion
minimal_context: Jennifer is participating in designated classroom reading time with the goal of reading a novel independently.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for independent reading. Please choose a novel from the shelf and read quietly at your desk.

STUDENT: (Spends a large amount of time looking through the books on the shelf without selecting one) My interest has gone down in middle school. I hate reading. Reading is boring.

TUTOR: Please just select a book and sit down to read.

STUDENT: (Sits down with a book and starts skimming the text pictures and captions instead of reading) Some of the words are hard. I don’t get it.

TUTOR: Keep reading and see if you can figure it out.

STUDENT: (Pushes the book away, completely disengaged) I get to the point that I barely understand it. I'm just confused by it.

options.A: Provide the one-on-one assistance of a paraprofessional during the independent reading time to help the student navigate the text.
options.B: Provide immediate and instructional feedback, helping the student to understand exactly what she should have done during the independent reading activity.
options.C: Use audio recordings of the text, chunking the reading into 10-minute sessions so the student can stop after each section to write thoughts and questions for discussion.
options.D: Agree with the student that she is having a rough time with the novel during this independent reading session.
